reason: Replaces an over-inferred compensation-flow claim with the exact RA 9266 IRR Section 36 fee-collection rule.

source_audit_support.quoted_pdf_excerpt: It shall be unlawful for any unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services except as an employee collecting a fee as representative of a Registered Architect.

proposed.text: Under RA 9266 IRR Section 36, what fee-collection rule applies to an unregistered person?

options.text: The person may collect architectural fees directly if the client agrees in writing
The person may not collect a fee for architectural services except as an employee representative of a Registered Architect
The person must collect fees through the Board, which distributes professional compensation
The person may collect fees after the project is completed, even without registration

rationale.a: Client agreement cannot override the statutory fee-collection rule.
rationale.b: Correct. Section 36 makes fee collection by an unregistered person unlawful except as an employee collecting as representative of a Registered Architect.
rationale.c: The Board does not act as a fee-distribution intermediary under Section 36.
rationale.d: Later collection does not cure lack of registration or authority.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 IRR Section 36 controls the fee-collection issue: an unregistered person cannot collect a fee for architectural services except through the stated employee-representative exception.
rationale.takeaway: Section 36: no direct architectural fee collection by unregistered persons, except the employee-representative case.
